output.summary: Jensen Hughes will review construction documents for the fire and intrusion alarm systems in the new Claremont Middle School multipurpose building, checking them against building, fire and State Architect rules and district standards. The limit of $28,000 includes a $6,200 contingency, and work runs from June 11, 2020 through December 31, 2023.

output.headline: Adds $675 to a contract for stage set design for Castlemont High School's drama production
output.summary: The district is ratifying an amendment to a professional services contract with an individual contractor who plans and builds stage designs with the art and drama departments for Castlemont High School's drama production. It adds $675.00 and raises the contract limit from $7,875.00 to $8,550.00 for August 14, 2019 through June 1, 2020. Ratification means the board is approving it after it has already begun.

output.headline: Leases classrooms at the former Rudsdale campus to Unity Middle School for about $56,281

money.evidence: anticipated revenue to the District of $56,281.42

output.summary: The district will let Unity Middle School, a charter school, use classrooms at the former Rudsdale Campus for the 2020-21 school year under Proposition 39. The district expects to receive $56,281.42 in return.

output.headline: Approves state charter school facilities agreement for Aspire Berkley Maynard Academy, no cost
output.summary: The district joins Aspire Public Schools and the State of California in a memorandum of understanding for a Proposition 51 school construction grant for Aspire Berkley Maynard Academy. The agreement has no direct cost to the district.

output.headline: Continues no-cost school food partnership with Center for Ecoliteracy through 2023
output.summary: The district and the Center for Ecoliteracy are signing a memorandum of understanding (MOU) to keep running the Rethinking School Lunch Oakland initiative over the next three years (2020-2023). The partnership began in 2011 and covers school food innovations and related educational programs. It is at no cost to the district.

output.headline: Adds $1,680 to a contract for a farm manager at Castlemont High School
output.summary: The board is approving more pay for a contractor who runs the school farm at Castlemont High School: 56 more hours for planting, harvesting and helping the farm supply food to the community during COVID-19. The contract limit rises from $20,000 to $21,680. The contract period began in August 2019, before this approval.

output.headline: Partners with Refugee Transitions; district would get $21,600 from Oakland youth fund
output.summary: The district's Refugee and Newcomer Program and Refugee Transitions agree to work together on the Newcomer Community Engagement Program. If the funding is awarded, the district will receive $21,600 from the Oakland Fund for Children and Youth for July 2019 through June 2020.

output.headline: Ratifies $19,000 for Entelo's virtual interview platform for hiring

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $19,000.00

output.summary: The district is approving after the work began a contract with Entelo, Inc. for a virtual interview platform, with on-demand and live interviews for up to 500 hires, up to fifteen recruiter seats, plus training and consulting. The cost is capped at $19,000.00 for January 20, 2020 through January 19, 2021. It is managed by the Talent/Human Resources Department.

output.headline: Ratifies $19,000 for Study.com test prep licenses for teacher candidates

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $19,000.00

output.summary: The district is approving after the work began a contract with Study.com for 150 licenses for study help and test preparation. They are for teacher candidates or teachers preparing for certification exams for a teaching credential. The cost is capped at $19,000.00 for April 30, 2020 through July 28, 2020.

output.headline: Pays KW Engineering $39,224 to check building systems design at Madison Park Academy
output.summary: KW Engineering will review and prepare design documents for commissioning, which makes sure building systems and controls work together properly and save operating costs, for the Madison Park Academy Expansion Project. The $39,224.40 includes a $1,324.40 contingency, and work runs from October 1 to December 31, 2020.

output.headline: Pays Safe Passages up to $10,000 for social work services at Laurel Elementary

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $10,000.00

output.summary: Safe Passages will provide 360 hours of case management and other social work services for students at Laurel Elementary School. The contract runs from January 20 to May 22, 2020, which began before the board approved it, and is paid from donations.

output.headline: Adds $573,781 and a year for Colland Jang Architecture project management services
output.summary: Colland Jang Architecture will keep providing project management for ongoing facilities projects, plus a cost estimator and a project manager. The contract limit rises from $576,103 to $1,149,884 and the end date moves from June 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $2.01M and a year for Cordoba construction management on facilities projects
output.summary: Cordoba Corporation will keep providing construction management services for the district's facilities projects. The contract limit rises from $4,118,572 to $6,128,007 and the end date moves from June 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $1,500 to build a Humanities 9 curriculum at Life Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $1,500.00

output.summary: A contractor worked with Life Academy teachers to build a ninth-grade Humanities curriculum that meets Common Core and Career Technical Education standards, with assessments of student mastery. The contract ran from January 13 to March 6, 2020, which began before this approval, and is paid with Measure N funds.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $1,475 to build Geometry and Statistics lessons at Life Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $1,475.00

output.summary: A contractor built Geometry and Statistics units and assessments for Life Academy that meet Common Core and Career Technical Education standards and go beyond the Illustrative Mathematics curriculum. The contract ran from February 18 to March 10, 2020, which began before this approval, and is paid with Measure N funds.

output.headline: Pays a consultant up to $2,000 to build Algebra 1 and 2 lessons at Life Academy

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $2,000.00

output.summary: A contractor built Algebra 1 and 2 units and assessments for Life Academy that meet Common Core and Career Technical Education standards and go beyond the Illustrative Mathematics curriculum. The contract ran from February 4 to March 6, 2020, which began before this approval, and is paid with Measure N funds.

output.headline: Accepts $100,000 from the Haas Fund to train 100 career pathway teachers in trauma care
output.summary: The Walter and Elise Haas Fund is giving the district $100,000 to train and coach 100 career pathway teachers in trauma-informed care, so they can support Oakland youth mental health after the impact of COVID-19. The High School Linked Learning Office will run the work from May 1, 2020 through June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Pays Street Academy Foundation up to $2,000 for distance-learning career courses

money.evidence: in an amount not to exceed $2,000.00

output.summary: Street Academy Foundation will develop Career Technical Education curriculum that can be taught through distance learning, working with the Linked Learning Department. The contract covers June 1 to June 30, 2020.

output.headline: Accepts $10,000 from Project Lead the Way for the engineering program at Oakland High
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district a $10,000 grant to help pay for its Project Lead the Way engineering program at Oakland High School. The grant period runs from February 13, 2020 through May 31, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $1.09M and a year for Cumming construction management on the Measure J bond program
output.summary: Cumming Management Group will keep providing construction management for the Measure J bond program. The contract limit rises from $2,024,705 to $3,115,305 and the end date moves from June 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Adds $190,000 and a year for School Facility Consultants to pursue state construction funding
output.summary: School Facility Consultants will keep helping the district find and apply for State funding for new school construction, modernization and joint-use projects. The contract limit rises from $190,000 to $380,000 and the end date moves from June 30, 2020 to June 30, 2021.

output.headline: Accepts $20,000 from Project Lead the Way for its Gateway program at Madison Park Academy
output.summary: Project Lead the Way, Inc. is giving the district a $20,000 grant to help pay for the Project Lead the Way Gateway program at Madison Park Academy (6-12). The grant period runs from February 13, 2020 through May 31, 2022.

output.headline: Moves $250,000 milk and dairy bid from closed Berkeley Farms to Crystal Creamery

money.evidence: in present amount not to exceed $250,000.00

output.summary: Berkeley Farms Dairy stopped doing business, so the district is moving its milk and dairy bid award to Crystal Creamery, the second-lowest responsive and responsible bidder. The amount is capped at $250,000.00 for the rest of the 2019-20 school year, with two one-year renewal options. The Superintendent already took this action, and the Board is being asked to ratify it.

output.headline: Accepts $97,500 from No Kid Hungry for grab-and-go meals during COVID-19
output.summary: The district is accepting a $97,500.00 grant from the No Kid Hungry Campaign. The money supports the Grab and Go Meal Distribution Program, which gives nutritious meals to kids and families during the COVID-19 emergency. The grant covers March 16, 2020 through June 30, 2020 and is managed by the Nutrition Services Department.

output.headline: Approves the minutes of the May 13, 2020 Board of Education meeting
output.summary: The board is approving the written record of its regular virtual meeting held on May 13, 2020. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. There is no cost.

output.headline: Creates five new job descriptions and revises one, mostly for Nutrition Services
output.summary: The Board is adopting a resolution that creates five job descriptions: Executive Chef/Production Manager; Supervisor, Central Kitchen Warehouse and Distribution; Specialist, Receiver/Inventory; Specialist, Food Logistics and Distribution; and Program Manager, Nutrition Services. It also revises the Director of Instruction, PreK-12 job description. The text states no dollar amount.
